Potential issues: PersistentDictionary::ValueOrDefault implementation.

In persistent_dictionary.h:
```
template <typename T>
T ValueOrDefault(const std::string_view key, T default_value) const {
  if (auto value = T{}; Get(key, &value))
    return value;
  return default_value;
}
```

Bug: It creates value = T{} then calls Get(key, &value). If Get fails, value remains default constructed, but we return default_value. That's okay? Actually if Get fails, we return default_value. Good.

But note: Get returns bool. If Get succeeds, we return value. That's fine.

But there is subtle bug: The template uses auto value = T{}; Get(key, &value). If Get succeeds but value is default-constructed? No.
